quickSummary: Enthalpy H = U + PV satisfies ΔH = ΔU + Δn_g RT. Hess's law establishes that total reaction enthalpy is path-independent: Δ_r H° = Σ ΔH_steps, evaluated using formation enthalpies, combustion enthalpies, or bond dissociation energies.
summary: Master enthalpy relations, standard thermochemical definitions, and the three operational calculation bridges of Hess's Law.

conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Fundamental Enthalpy Relation**:
$$\mathbf{\Delta H = \Delta U + \Delta(PV) = \Delta U + \Delta n_g R T}$$
where $\Delta n_g = \sum n_g (\text{gaseous products}) - \sum n_g (\text{gaseous reactants})$.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 4.2 Hess's Law & The Three Operational Bridges
conceptBreakdown.title: 4.2 Hess's Law & The Three Operational Bridges
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
HESS'S LAW APPLICATIONS
                          
   1. From Formation Enthalpies:  Δ_r H° = Σ ν_p Δ_f H°(products) - Σ ν_r Δ_f H°(reactants)
   2. From Combustion Enthalpies: Δ_r H° = Σ ν_r Δ_c H°(reactants) - Σ ν_p Δ_c H°(products)
   3. From Bond Enthalpies:       Δ_r H° = Σ B.E.(reactants broken) - Σ B.E.(products formed)
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Hess's Law**: The net enthalpy change of a chemical reaction is identical whether the process occurs in one single step or through a series of intermediate steps:
$$\mathbf{\Delta_r H^\circ = \sum \Delta H_{\text{step } i}}$$

Δ_f H° of Ozone (O₃(g)) = +142.7 kJ/mol (NOT zero!).
